messages:
inc-bot: ALERT: Multiple AZ/network anomalies detected affecting EU and EU-west-2 frontends. Automatic regional failover started. pager: paged maria.

maria (oncall): I’m on it. seeing elevated 502/504s from eu cluster, latency spikes. grabbing logs.

jordan (eng-infra): Confirming: control-plane health looks OK, but edge pods in eu-west-2 are flapping and we have partial BGP withdraws from one AZ. routing% across region = unstable.

kai (network): Provider reported a partial network fabric degradation in eu-west-2b, some load-balancer nodes not re-advertising routes. DNS still healthy but some frontends not responding to probe.

maria (oncall): Triggered traffic-shift to eu-west-1 as per runbook to reduce customer impact. Traffic shift started at 1785004340.

tara (support): We’ve received 12 customer reports of timeouts and degraded inference latency, mostly EU users. CS notified.

jordan (eng-infra): Shift hit a snag — our traffic-shift controller shows stuck replica count at 60% because target autoscaler didn't spin up enough warm instances; autoscaler logs show failed warms: "quota exceeded" errors.

maria (oncall): Hmm, that would cause uneven routing and some requests hitting drained nodes. Increasing target capacity manually as hotfix.

ops-bot: Deploy started: increase-dedicated-pool-eu-west-1 - diff: +12 instances (initiated by maria).

alex (prod): Running quick smoke: curl -v https://eu.api.redwood.ai/health -> intermittent 504s still. dig @8.8.8.8 eu.api.redwood.ai -> returns both eu-west-2 and eu-west-1 IPs, TTL=60.

kai (network): DNS ok; problem is some eu-west-2 frontends still advertising and getting small fraction of traffic. But the backend routing inside provider is dropping sessions when they failover mid-stream.

jordan (eng-infra): Rolling back some failover automation flags to force full cutover. executing: 
```
kubectl annotate svc/traffic-shift controller.redwood/force-cutover=true --overwrite
```

maria (oncall): Also flushing edge connection caches to avoid stale next-hops. running provider console command to flush LB connection table (sent).

tara (support): Drafting status update for customers: short note about regional network incident, mitigation in progress, ETA ~30-45m. Any material data loss?

alex (prod): No data loss. Some requests retried by clients succeeded, but error rate increased to ~8% in EU for the last 15m. We likely will miss 99th pct latency SLO during incident window.

kai (network): Provider update: full convergence expected in ~20 mins after cache flush. They also suggested BGP reroute which we requested.

jordan (eng-infra): After force-cutover, traffic percent to eu-west-2 dropped from 18% -> 2% over ~3 minutes. Backend error rate in eu dropped accordingly.

maria (oncall): Monitoring metrics: overall requests per second normalized, errors trending down. Keeping canary routes for 5 mins before full restore.

ops-bot: Incident timeline note appended to ticket INC-1785004321.

tara (support): Customer comms sent: Support acknowledges and explains failover; asked customers to open tickets if persistent.

alex (prod): Post-mortem notes so far: root cause likely partial provider network fabric failure in a single AZ that caused route fragmentation + autoscaler quota prevented smooth warm-up, leading to sticky sessions across partial failover.

jordan (eng-infra): Action items: (1) add pre-warm capacity guardrail for region failover, (2) update controller to detect "stuck shift" state and escalate automatically, (3) add runbook step to flush LB conn table earlier.

kai (network): Also request provider follow-up for why LB nodes kept advertising after partial fabric loss. Opening a support case and asking for detailed BGP dumps.

maria (oncall): Handoff: I’ll stay for the next 30m to verify steady state, then hand to oncall-night (jordan) at shift end. If errors go above 2% we re-escalate.

ops-bot: Oncall handoff scheduled at 1785007000 -> jordan (eng-infra).

maria (oncall): Final check: latency back to near-normal for EU users, error rate <1.5% last 5m. Declaring mitigation successful for now; postmortem to be authored.

tara (support): Notifying enterprise customers impacted with post-incident summary + interim mitigations.

alex (prod): Saving logs, snapshots, and setting replay window for ~2 hours to help postmortem.

inc-bot: STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Please file P1 postmortem and link here.

maria (oncall): Filed PM: https://internal.redwood/pms/1785004321 - will include timeline, root cause analysis, customer impact metrics and next steps.

jordan (eng-infra): Adding final note: we should simulate partial AZ withdraws in chaos lab to prevent repeat.

maria (oncall): thanks all. handing off to jordan for overnight watch.

jordan (eng-infra): taking over. ping me if anything spikes.
